solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Children's amusement to come out at the end of spring

definitions.text: Children's amusement to come out at the end of spring

parts.words: Children's amusement to come out at the end of spring
parts.note: a toy figure that pops up out of its box on the end of a coiled spring when the lid is opened

explanation.surface: Kids enjoying a day out once spring is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' reads as the season, so 'the end of spring' sounds like early summer; it is the coiled spring the toy figure sits on.
explanation.definitionFit: The toy is a clown head mounted on a coil that leaps from its case when the catch is released.

clue.text: Heartless pranks on pensioner one picked on

indicators.note: losing its heart means the middle letter of the word for pranks is dropped

parts.note: jokes are pranks
OAP stands for old-age pensioner

explanation.surface: Cruel tricks played on an old person who gets bullied.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartless' takes the middle K out of JOKES, leaving JOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Joe Soap is a British name for an ordinary person who gets landed with the dull or unfair jobs, a dupe or scapegoat.

clue.text: Helmsman, crossing bridge finally, first to get on

indicators.note: the steersman's word goes across, straddling the letter taken from the bridge

parts.note: a cox steers a rowing boat

indicators.note: only the last letter of the word bridge is wanted here

parts.note: 1ST, with I standing for the figure one

explanation.surface: A steersman crossing a bridge is the first to board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' as a number is 1ST, with the figure 1 read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: To coexist is to live alongside others peaceably, which is what people who get on do.

clue.text: Popular article by expert revealing all

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the is the definite article
a buff is an enthusiast with expert knowledge

explanation.surface: A hit piece written by a specialist exposes everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in the buff means naked, with nothing concealed from view.

clue.text: Credit's what you give correct answers!

definitions.meaning: on tick means on credit, so ... here are credit arrangements
a marker puts a check mark beside each right answer

explanation.definitionFit: Tick is informal British for credit, and a tick is also the check mark awarded to a right answer.

clue.text: Solve old jumbo you've picked up?

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: something picked up is heard, so the word for jumbo is replaced by one that sounds the same

parts.note: a jumbo jet is a plane

explanation.surface: Can you work out how you collected an old jumbo jet?
explanation.walkthrough: 'picked up' swaps PLANE for PLAIN, which sounds identical; 'you've' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To explain a puzzle or mystery is to make it clear, which amounts to solving it.

clue.text: Lack of transparency — and compassion — when handling bill

parts.note: O, zero, signals a complete lack

indicators.note: to handle is to hold in the hands, so the compassion piece wraps round the bill

parts.note: pity is compassion
AC, account, is a bill

explanation.surface: Murkiness, and kindness, when dealing with an invoice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lack' does double duty: part of the definition and also O (nothing); 'handling' puts AC inside OPITY.
explanation.definitionFit: Opacity is the quality of being opaque: light cannot pass through, the reverse of transparency.

clue.text: Jargon taken down — an unknown amount to work out

parts.note: food gobbled is swallowed, taken down
Y is an algebraic unknown
go can mean total, as in what the bill goes to
something that works out is OK

explanation.surface: Technical talk is noted down, leaving an unspecified sum to calculate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken down' reads as written down from dictation but means swallowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Gobbledygook is pompous unintelligible language, as jargon often seems to outsiders.

clue.text: Stuff concluded each time

parts.note: over means finished

explanation.surface: Things that were finished every time.
explanation.definitionFit: To stuff yourself is to eat too much, a verb sense of stuff.

clue.text: Cook, perhaps, better back at home

parts.note: to cap something is to better it

indicators.note: back says the little word at is to be read the other way round

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: A chef who is better back in their own kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cook' is the explorer Captain James Cook, not a chef; 'back' turns AT into TA.
explanation.definitionFit: James Cook, the explorer, held the naval rank of captain, so he is an example of one.

clue.text: I'm messing with chap? No, many!

definitions.text: I'm messing with chap? No, many!

indicators.note: messing with something jumbles it, so these letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: A woman declares she is not seeing one man but lots of them.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the speaker's boast.
explanation.definitionFit: A nymphomaniac, in the old usage, was a woman with uncontrollable sexual appetite, wanting many partners.

clue.text: Soothing words remain in the memory? On the contrary

indicators.note: in places one word inside another, here the memory word and the remain word
this flips the order the clue states, so the remain word holds the memory word instead

parts.note: to bide is to remain
ROM is computer read-only memory

explanation.surface: Comforting phrases stick in the mind, or is it the other way round?
explanation.walkthrough: Taken literally the clue puts the remain word inside the memory word; 'On the contrary' says the containment runs the other way.
explanation.definitionFit: A bromide is a platitude meant to calm, after the bromide salts once used as sedatives.

clue.text: Admit us for sport here?

indicators.note: done for sport means for fun, playfully, so the letters are toyed with

explanation.surface: Fans at the gate asking to be let in to watch the game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for sport' is the anagram signal, and also the reason for the visit.
explanation.definitionFit: A stadium is the arena where spectators are let in to watch sporting events.

clue.text: Video maybe looking back, by visiting foreign resident

indicators.note: a visitor goes into a place, so one piece enters the other
looking back says the video word runs from right to left

parts.note: a video tape, so tape is an example
X as in multiplication, two by three

explanation.surface: Watching a video as a reminder while abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looking back' turns TAPE into EPAT; 'visiting' puts X inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An expat (expatriate) lives in a country other than their own.

clue.text: Rocky hurt by man one shouldn't trust?

indicators.note: rocky means unstable, so these letters are unsettled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Rocky Balboa beaten by an opponent who cannot be trusted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rocky' looks like the boxer's name; it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An urban myth is a widely repeated but untrue story, so not to be relied on.

clue.text: Performing with idol in Birmingham: that takes some beating!

indicators.note: in places the performing and idol pieces within the city's nickname

parts.note: Brum is the informal name for Birmingham, an English city
on means on stage, performing
an idol is a false god

explanation.surface: A pop idol on stage in Birmingham: an unbeatable show!
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes some beating' sounds like praise; the drum is literally beaten. BRUM is the local nickname for Birmingham.
explanation.definitionFit: A bongo drum is a small hand drum played by striking with the fingers.

clue.text: Bursting with life — only there's a large catch

indicators.note: bursting breaks something apart, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A lively angler, except there's a big fish on the line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bursting' shuffles W, LIFE and ONLY; 'there's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Yellowfin is a large tuna prized by sea anglers and commercial fishers.

clue.text: Motorists commandeering stern of cruise ship: that we've never understood!

indicators.note: to commandeer is to seize, so the motorists' letters take over the ship's stern

parts.note: a liner is a passenger ship

indicators.note: the stern is the back of a ship, so the last letter is meant

parts.note: the AA, the Automobile Association, is a British motoring organisation

explanation.surface: Drivers hijacking the back of a cruise liner: baffling!
explanation.walkthrough: AA surround the R at the stern of LINER, giving LINE + ARA.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear A is a Minoan script found on Cretan clay tablets that has never been deciphered.

clue.text: Treat with powerful agent organised in European zoos

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European, followed by zoos as written

explanation.surface: Animals in European zoos get treated with a strong drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Ozone is a strong oxidising gas, and to ozonise something is to treat it with that gas.

clue.text: Doubt and unease in equal measure

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the phrase that follows

explanation.surface: Feeling equally unsure and uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: A qualm is a pang of misgiving or uneasy conscience.

clue.text: Band give shows — and live!

parts.note: both give and live contain the Roman numeral IV, four, so the band is a four-piece

explanation.surface: A group that plays live gigs.
explanation.walkthrough: IV, Roman four, sits in both 'give' and 'live'; a group of four players is the band.
explanation.definitionFit: A quartet is a group of four musicians or singers performing together.

clue.text: A story, and not one to pass on legally

parts.note: a story can be a fib or lie
nor means and not

explanation.surface: A tale about someone who should not hand things on through the courts.
explanation.definitionFit: In law an alienor is the party who transfers property or title to someone else.

clue.text: Defender's regret, perhaps, to have ambition

parts.note: to own is to have
a goal is an ambition

explanation.surface: A footballer regrets being ambitious.
explanation.walkthrough: In football, a defender who puts the ball into their own net has scored an own goal.
explanation.definitionFit: Scoring into one's own net is a classic blunder by a defender, hence 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Commentator's not in time for West Ham's match

indicators.note: a commentator speaks, so what follows is heard rather than read
West Ham is in east London, so a Cockney accent is meant

parts.note: late means not in time

explanation.surface: A broadcaster arrives late for a West Ham football game.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham is an east London club; in a Cockney accent LATE is said like LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: A match is something that gives a light, as in asking someone for a light.

clue.text: Hand over tax I owe? Not at first

parts.note: O is the cricket abbreviation for over
VAT is value added tax

indicators.note: at first asks for only the opening letters of the two words before it

explanation.surface: Pass on the tax I owe? Not at the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hand' is applause, as in 'give them a big hand'.
explanation.definitionFit: A big hand is a round of applause, and an ovation is enthusiastic applause.

clue.text: Crime writer's conclusion to book worrying

indicators.note: the conclusion is the end, so the last letter of book

parts.note: eating as in what's eating you, worrying

explanation.surface: A mystery author's ending to a book is disturbing.
explanation.walkthrough: ''s' is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: H. R. F. Keating wrote the Inspector Ghote detective novels.

clue.text: Building's bar area storing large quantity of beer?

indicators.note: storing means holding within, so one piece contains another

parts.note: a rod is a bar
a tun is a large cask for beer or wine

explanation.surface: A pub's bar holds a huge barrel of beer.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a round building, usually domed.

clue.text: Warning is hollow — a bait, otherwise

parts.note: a cave is a hollow
to bait is to lure or tempt
or means otherwise

explanation.surface: An empty threat: a trap, or something else.
explanation.definitionFit: Latin for 'let the buyer beware', a caution that purchasers bear the risk.
